text: {"question":"How does the behavior of the effective dark‑energy component in the GPAges models, particularly the negative ΩX values at intermediate redshifts and the divergence of wX near z∼40–60 and z∼2–3, influence the assessment of Hubble‑constant tension when compared to the suite of fourteen alternative ΛCDM extensions evaluated in the updated H0 World Cup?","reference_answer":"The negative ΩX in GPAges implies an effective excess of matter at 2≲z≲60, which would alter the late‑time expansion rate and could reduce the inferred H0 from CMB+BAO data, thereby tightening the H0 tension. The divergences in wX at z∼40–60 and z∼2–3 introduce rapid changes in the expansion history that are not captured by the other late‑time or early‑time extensions in the H0 World Cup, making GPAges a distinct candidate that could either alleviate or exacerbate the tension depending on the precise fit to the combined datasets.","passage_1_contribution":"GPAges predicts a negative ΩX at intermediate redshifts and divergent wX near z∼40–60 and z∼2–3, indicating significant deviations from ΛCDM in the expansion history.","passage_2_contribution":"The H0 World Cup evaluates fourteen alternative models to ΛCDM, including late‑time modifications, to address the Hubble tension using CMB, BAO, and SN data.","joint_reason":"Both passages discuss how deviations from ΛCDM affect the expansion history and the Hubble constant; combining GPAges’ specific predictions with the broader model comparison framework allows assessment of its impact on the H0 tension.","same_quantity":false}
